:::{#cor-joint-density-mass-marginal}
#### Marginal PMF from a joint density-mass function

If $X$ and $Y$ have joint density-mass function $\p(X = x,\, Y = y)$,
then for every $x$:

$$\P(X = x) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \p(X = x,\, Y = y)\,dy$$

:::

::: proof

Every outcome has $Y(\outcome) \in \reals$,
so $\set{Y \in \reals} = \samplespace$, and:

$$
\ba
\P(X = x)
&= \Pr(\set{X = x} \cap \samplespace)
&& \text{(} \set{X = x} \subseteq \samplespace \text{)} \\
&= \Pr(X = x,\, Y \in \reals)
&& \text{(} \set{Y \in \reals} = \samplespace \text{)} \\
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \p(X = x,\, Y = y)\,dy
&& \text{(definition of a joint density-mass function, with } B = \reals \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
